institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to do my exchange in Vienna mainly because I wanted to go to a German speaking country to improve my German. Furthermore also a city close to nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been a very nice experience, and I have met some fantastic people during my exchange! For the personal and social part, it has really been an  10/10 experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest to find all the information upon arrival. I spend quite some time researching and asking for help to plan my exchange - but I guess it is a part of the exchange process... I wish I have had some kind of physical info-meeting, where you could ask questions in person. I think that would have made it so much more easier, instead of writing emails back and forth. I know some of my friends had a physical info-meeting, but I sadly did not get any information about a meeting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Even before my arrival, I got connected with a buddy from BOKU university. It was really nice, so I had the chance to ask her more specific questions about the study life and the courses. The first week was an introduction week, so it was nice to get all the information in person, and be introduced to the exchange coordinators.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Sometimes I had to wait quite some time for having my emails answered from the exchange coordinator.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I sent a lot of applications before finding a place to live, so I would recommend to begin early. I used the housing webpage WGgesucht - there is a lot of nice flat shares (WGs) in Vienna!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live off campus, to explore other parts of the city. I would recommend not to live too far away from BOKU, maybe max. 30 min. I rented a bike so that I could bike 20 min to school (but be aware that BOKU is on the top of a hill..;))

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration for the school was easy, but you have to show up in person when you arrive. The registration of the courses was very confusing...

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To register at BOKU you have to show up in person when you arrive, and pay a small amount for being registered. You have to be registered in person at the school, before you can register for any courses. This is a bit annoying, because then you can only start registering for courses kind of late before semester start, and therefore a lot of courses are already filled up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I asked my exchange coordinator at BOKU, but she told me that it is very normal to be on waiting list for courses, and also to have overlaps between courses. I also asked my roomies, buddy and other Erasmus students for help in the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: When I registered, there were already a lot of the courses that were filled up, because too many students registered in the courses. I was on the waiting list for a lot of courses. I was not really satisfied with this process, because it was a bit stressful not to be sure which courses I would get, and to make the puzzle of a schedule so that the courses would not overlap too much.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If it is possible, I would maybe arrive 1-2 weeks before the semester starts, to have time to make the schedule. Then I would make a long list of courses, so there is both a plan A, B and C... Sometimes you can also ask the professor by mail or by entering the first class, if there should be a place free anyway, if you are on the waiting list for courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not have many courses from the landscape architecture bachelor programme, because most of them are in German, or there was not enough places. I think most of my courses were interesting, but the number of the ECTS for the courses were not at all appropriate. In many courses the work load was way too high compared to the low number of ECTS.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think some of the master courses were a bit difficult, but also because it was a bit in another studyfield than I have. For example I had a master course in climate change that was really interesting, but also challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It really depends on the course... Some of the lectures were a bit more monologue than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Biocultural diversity in rural landscapes (eng.)
- Biodiversity and conservation of mountain forests (eng.)
- Climate change and global aspects in planning and spatial development (eng.)
- Deutsch Konversation III (ger.)
- Deutsche Fachsprache B (B2+) (ger.)
- Einführung in den Möbel- und Innenausbau (ger.)
- Exkursion Verkehrswesen (ger.)
- Fish farming and aquaculture (eng.)
- Freies Zeichnen (ger.)
- Gehölzkunde (ger.)
- Introduction to urbanism (eng.)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend to choose some more easy courses if possible. It is really difficult so find enough courses to fill 30 ECTS, so I think it is important not to stress yourself too much with too many difficult courses! 
I would recommend the Freies Zeichnen course, if you like to draw. It is a very nice course that is only for one week, where you go to the city centre to draw architecture and plants. 
If you are interested in plants, then I would really recommend the Gehölzkunde course. Even though it is in German, is there a lot of the same words to describe plants as in danish. There is a lot of plants to learn though!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy climbing shoes for a climbing course I took. I also had a fine for not being registered in Vienna (remember to do that).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not have to buy a lot of books for uni. Only a scriptum for one course, and some drawing materials for another course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took a climbing course at the USI. They have a lot of different courses available for the semester!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: BOKU has a lot of social events! There is a student driven cafe/bar/shop and they are also organizing events and parties. Keep an eye on the posters hanging around at BOKU with all sort of events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Really nice to do a sport, also a possibility to meet new people. There is also a WhatsApp-group for Erasmus and incoming students - here they will also write about events and parties:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of nice museums in Vienna! Look out for free entrances, some days you can be lucky to get in for free. The music and theatre scene in Vienna is also very big. Vienna is also very close to beautiful nature: The Nationalpark Donau Auen, Donau Insel - where you can swim in the Donau river, The Wiener Wald and the nearby "hills" or mountains where you can easily access with some 1,5-2 hours of train. There is a lot of hiking routes from Vienna - called Stadtwanderwege. 
Last but not least is there a lot of neighbor countries to Vienna! It is quite cheap and easy to go to f.x. Bratislava, Budapest and Prague.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the viennese people are very calm and mostly very nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take part in local events, play sports ect.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some waiters can be a bit grumpy, but this is supposed to be the style as far as I know.. Remember to give tips!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That the Austrians do not stress so much and like to go out to eat and drink coffee.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Take your time to do the registration and all the bureaucratic stuff... Even though it can feel stressful because of the deadlines, do not worry - it will be fine and work out!
- Participate in the introduction week! It is such a good way to meet new people and make new friends:)
- Ask as many questions as you want if you are in doubt of something. Ask BOKU, buddy, other Erasmus students, your roomies ect.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met at BOKU and the social life at campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bureaucratic stuff was a big challenge, but I think I also learned something from it..

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is really nice and rewarding to try and study in another country! Good luck :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
